properties.areaDesc: Metro Palm Beach County; Metro Broward County; Metropolitan Miami Dade; Coastal Palm Beach County; Coastal Broward County; Coastal Miami Dade County
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 24 at 11:25PM EST until November 26 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain.

Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 4-6 inches of rain. A few
locations could see 10 or more inches of rain.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

the Haines Highway decreasing down towards the Haines Borough to
around 2 to 4 inches.

* WHERE...Haines Borough, Klukwan, and Haines Border Crossing

* WHEN...Until 3 AM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. Travel could be
difficult.

Highway to now include the Haines Borough and Chilkat Peninsula.
FAA and 411 AKDOT cameras indicate moderate to heavy snowfall is
ongoing with visibilities around 1 mile or less.

currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM EST
Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 4 AM EST
Wednesday through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.

to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday
to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf
Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings.

Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

Virgin Islands, along the northern exposed beaches of St.

return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.description:

...COASTAL FLOOD STATEMENT IN EFFECT FOR ALL HAWAIIAN ISLANDS...

.A large, long-period north-northwest swell has likely peaked at
the offshore buoys, and the resultant surf will peak overnight and
then subside Wednesday. An even larger north-northwest swell is
likely Wednesday night into Thursday. Higher than predicted water
levels could lead to flooding of beaches that typically remain
dry, particularly during the pre-dawn high tides Wednesday and
Thursday mornings.

ramps and other coastal infrastructure of all Hawaiian islands.

* WHEN...From 6 PM HST this evening through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of beaches that are normally dry, minor
coastal erosion, and saltwater inundation.
properties.instruction:

higher ground. Monitor vessels to ensure mooring lines don't get
too tight and watch out for overwash around boat ramps. Secure
canoes or other watercraft stowed on beaches.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 24 at 5:58PM CST until November 25 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Statement,
isolated minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Wednesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday afternoon.
For the Coastal Flood Statement, through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow
beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could
be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may
experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also
occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State
Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 60 mph possible.

* WHERE...In Oregon, Clatsop County Coast and Tillamook County Coast.
In Washington, South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are possible. Travel could be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
properties.instruction:
Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location prior to
the onset of winds.

Consider sleeping in a location that is furthest away from large
trees and power lines. Be aware of your surroundings and where you
are relative to nearby trees and powerlines.

Prepare for potential power outages. If you have a gas-powered
generator, ensure you have enough fuel. Ensure you have batteries,
flashlights, and a way to maintain a safe body temperature if you
were to lose heating and cooling.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 24 at 1:10PM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Tidal levels across the panhandle are expected to be running high
for the next few days. These high tides combined with passing low
pressures and their associated fronts could create some
potentially higher than normal water levels. Wind direction,
magnitude, and timing with these systems will be monitored closely as
a combination of high tide and winds in an onshore direction
could lead to tides exceeding astronomical high tide by a foot or
more.

properties.areaDesc: Southern New Haven; Bronx; Northwest Suffolk; Northern Queens; Northern Nassau
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 4:57PM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...1 1/2 to 2 1/2 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...In Connecticut, Southern New Haven County. In New
York, Bronx, Northwest Suffolk, Northern Queens and Northern
Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning through Friday afternoon high
tides.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including
roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses
with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are
likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also
extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 3 to 6 ft will result in
areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave
splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable
structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is
potential for isolated damage to shoreline and marina
structures as well.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially
extending into the Friday afternoon high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide
a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is
quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast
could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if
slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.
properties.instruction:

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 24 at 1:57PM PST until November 27 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, now through 1 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM
PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9-
8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back
in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long
period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a
sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday.
Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10
feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by
Friday morning's high tide.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 1:42PM PST until November 25 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal flooding
with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, from 6 AM to 4 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW)
at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. The alignment of high surf and high tide will
increase the combined hazard significantly on Wednesday. These
predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through
the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 1:27PM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas. Up to 1 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major
flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 1.0
foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in
low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves up to 25 feet. Surf may
worsen coastal flooding along exposed beaches.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 AM to 7 PM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Thursday morning
through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to sections of
Highways 101 and 1. Shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to
rival the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant coastal impacts.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 24 at 1:24PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 121 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed 11/25, +2.5
ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.2 ft MHHW
(7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM Tue
11/24, +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed 11/25, +2.3
ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.1 ft MHHW
(6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Tue 11/24,
+7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.4 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27 and +7.0 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/28.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

consider altering their plans.

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 4:14PM EST until November 27 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 9 to 13 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 10 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of
vehicles will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be
inundated, especially around high tide. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor to moderate impacts forecast
Wednesday morning with the potential for more significant
impacts on Thursday morning. This will be of greatest concern
across the more vulnerable dunes along Hwy 12. However as winds
switch to a SW direction Thursday afternoon minor water level
rises (around 1-2 ft) on soundside locations.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 25 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Western portions of north central Texas.

* WHEN...From 11 PM this evening to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
properties.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and
unfrozen water.

Protect the 4 Ps from cold temperatures: People, pets, pipes, plants.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 1:10PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday Nov 30.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 110 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
